messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Sleep duration variable problem
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Sleep duration variable problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi Victoria,

acc_SPTDuration refers to the Sleep Period Time window, the window
between sleep onset and waking up in the morning.
The other variable refers to the accumulates sleep in that time
window. Humans, and I guess other mammals too, have a tendency to have
episodes of (neurological) wakefulness during their sleep, which we
usually do not consciously remember when we wake up in the morning.
The more you have these the poorer the sleep. However, 51 minutes
means very poor sleep. If this is result is very surprising for your
population then maybe:
- look at the visualreport of the data as that sometimes gives a hint
at what may be wrong... did the person wear the sensor during the
nights for example.
- check all other GGIR output to see how the measurement relative to
other individuals.

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
www.movementdata.nl <http://www.movementdata.nl>

On Fri, 17 Jan 2020 at 07:03, Victoria O’Callaghan
<victoria....@hotmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> I'm having trouble with the duration variable in my analyses. I am confused as to the difference between the variable 'acc_SPTDuration' in part 4 and 'dur_nightsleep_min' in part 5.  I've seen in the package manual that the latter is labelled as sleep duration but I have had some subjects with a value as low as 51 minutes (even though they went to bed at 19:07 and woke at 4:56). Why are the two variables sometimes so different and which one should I use for sleep duration?
>
> Thank you for you help!
>
> Victoria
>

messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] problem comparing analyses with relyonsleeplog = TRUE/FALSE
messages.body_plain:
Hi Morten,
 relyonsleeplog = FALSE, does make your analysis not depend on the sleeplog. It has a different function (see tutorial).

You should do the following instead:
loglocation = c(),
def.noc.sleep=c(1),

Vincent

messages.subject: Differences in estimated dur_nightsleep in Part5 output between GGIR 1.9-1 and 1.11-0
messages.subject_clean: Differences in estimated dur_nightsleep in Part5 output between GGIR 1.9-1 and 1.11-0
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I was wondering if anyone has the following issues when using 1.11-0 version:

1) Looking at the Part 5 day output from the analysis of Axivity AX3 file (cwa file), I noticed that the dur_night_sleep for the first 24h monitoring day (the second row of the output; see attached example) was much shorter with the 1.11-0 than 1.9-1 version (184.25 vs 518.5). It seems like the new version of GGIR did not include the midnight-wake up period into the calculation of sleep duration. Can someone please advise what could be the reason for that? I have attached is the config file which I used to run on both versions of GGIR.

2) I also spotted an error on Part5 output's timestamp with the 1.11-0 on my recent batch of GENEActiv data analysis. For example, the first day of recording data is 19/3/20; however, the timestamp recorded for Day 1 on Part5 output was 18/3/20. I re-run the analysis with the older version of GGIR and confirmed that I didn't make a mistake when initializing the monitors.

ps. I have accidentally updated my GGIR on RStudio and was wondering if there is a way for me to use the older version instead to ensure consistency in my analysis?

Thanks and best regards,
John.

messages.body_plain:
Hello Joanne,

I am also getting more of these kind of messages in the last couple of months. I agree that they are not very informative, so an area for improvement.

The error relates to a bit of code at the very end of GGIR part 1, which may indicate that part 2 can still run. Can you try to run part 2, 3, 4, 5 of GGIR? (argument mode = 2:5)

Another approach could be to see whether you could reproduce the problem by re-processing your data in a new output folder.  My feeling is that GGIR is more likely to be confused when data is processed in different stages while some details of the R script or the location of folders changes in between those stages.

Best, Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Using the sleep log for the sleep period time window to calculate sleep efficiency
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Using the sleep log for the sleep period time window to calculate sleep efficiency
messages.body_plain:
Hi Aron,
Good question, I see two approaches:
- Calculate it yourself per night by dividing sleep duration as part of SPT by the sleeplog defined SPT window duration. This will not change the person level aggregates, so maybe not exactly what you want.
- Set relyonsleeplog = TRUE, see also documentation: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/GGIR.pdf
Cheers,
Vincent

messages.subject_clean: Part5_daysummary activity duration in the day
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am confused by the output from the part5_daysummary csv. file (I attached one example output).

My understanding is that "dur_day_LIG30_100_min" is time spent in unbouted light activity during the day, while "dur_LIGB_D...T30_100_min" is time spent in bouted light activity during the day. So adding up these variables would be the total time spent in light activity during the day (which would be the variable "dur_TLIGday_min"). However, the sum of the unbouted and bouted values did not equals to the "dur_TLIGday_min" ("dur_day_LIG30_100_min"+"dur_LIGB_D10T30_100_min" + "dur_LIGB_D5T30_100_min" + "dur_LIGB_D1T30_100_min"  <  "dur_TLIGday_min"). The is the same for moderate activity.

On the contrary, adding up "dur_day_SIB_min", "dur_day_OIN30_min", "dur_INB_D30T30_min", "dur_INB_D10T30_min" and "dur_INB_D1T30_min" > "dur_TINday_min". The missing in total light and moderate activity = the extra in TIN.

I wonder why some inactivity would be regarded as light or moderate activity at the end? Do anyone have any ideas about it? Thank you!

Anjo

So adding up these variables would be the total time spent in light activity during the day (which would be the variable "dur_TLIGday_min"). messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GENEActiv .csv epoch file
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] GENEActiv .csv epoch file
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,
Thanks for your amazing work!
You previously mentioned that raw data should be recorded more than 20 Hertz. And I know that if the raw data is too small, the programme may not recognize it.
Our raw data were all collected with a measurement frequency at 10 Hertz. I tried to .bin file and could generate results with GGIR (.csv can not, maybe it's relatively small).
I'm just wondering  if GGIR could analyze data collected at 10 Hertz and would the measurement frequency affect results?
Looking forward to your reply. Thank you very much!

Regards,
Laura
